item.title: China honors international contributors to cultural exchange
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-21
China honors international contributors to cultural exchange Li Shulei, a member of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee and head of the Publicity Department of the CPC Central Committee, attends the 2026 Orchid Awards ceremony and delivers a speech in Beijing, capital of China, Nov. 20, 2026. (Xinhua/Zhang Ling) BEIJING, Nov. 20 (Xinhua) -- China on Friday honored French Nobel laureate in literature Jean-Marie Gustave Le Clézio, renowned Singaporean scholar Kishore Mahbubani, and eight other foreign nationals with its Orchid Awards, recognizing their efforts in facilitating cultural exchanges between China and the rest of the world. The 2026 Orchid Awards ceremony, the third of its kind, was held in Beijing. Li Shulei, a member of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee and head of the Publicity Department of the CPC Central Committee, attended the ceremony and delivered a speech. More than 300 people, including representatives of Chinese governmental departments, international organizations, diplomatic envoys in China, and Chinese and foreign think tanks and media organizations, attended Friday's event in the national capital. Participants stressed equality and inclusiveness among different civilizations, calling for efforts to preserve, inherit and pass on human civilizations, and to strengthen digital empowerment to make the progress of civilizations beneficial to all and shared by all. At a regular news briefing, Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun congratulated the award recipients, praising their long-term efforts in helping dispel prejudice through culture, deepening understanding via exchange and building people-to-people bridges between China and other countries. The Orchid Awards, established in 2022, aim to recognize international friends and organizations for outstanding contributions to promoting humanity's shared values and mutual learning between Chinese and foreign civilizations. They have become an international cultural platform helping implement the China-proposed Global Civilization Initiative. Copyright © 2026 People's Daily Online. All Rights Reserved.

item.title: China's intelligent computing expected to top 90 pct of total computing capacity
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-21
China's intelligent computing expected to top 90 pct of total computing capacity CHANGSHA, Nov. 20 (Xinhua) -- The 2026 World Computing Conference, which opened Friday in central China's Hunan Province, unveiled 10 major trends in China's computing power development, including a growing share for intelligent computing and faster building of a nationwide integrated computing network. Liu Wenqiang, vice president of the China Center for Information Industry Development, a co-organizer of the conference, said that by 2030, China's intelligent computing capacity is expected to approach 10,000 EFLOPS, or more than 90 percent of the country's total, with inference computing accounting for 85 percent of the intelligent computing mix. EFLOPS refers to a unit measuring computing performance, with each unit representing 1 quintillion floating-point operations per second. According to Liu, China's progress in computing power development is reflected mainly in the continued expansion of overall scale, the ongoing optimization of regional distribution and a steady strengthening of self-reliance capacity. As of the end of September 2026, the country's intelligent computing capacity stood at 2,592 EFLOPS, up 146 percent year on year, with 52 intelligent computing facilities each with more than 10,000 AI chips. A framework of eight national computing hubs, 10 national data center clusters and three regions for coordinated development of computing and energy has taken shape. The 10 major trends also include evaluation of green computing shifting from energy efficiency to carbon efficiency, and space computing moving from validation to networking, with China expected to build a 1,000-satellite commercial space computing network by 2030. item.title: China's high-tech FDI posts strong growth in first 10 months
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-21
China's high-tech FDI posts strong growth in first 10 months A drone photo taken on Nov. 19, 2026 shows a ship arriving at Rizhao Port in east China's Shandong Province. (Xinhua/Guo Xulei) BEIJING, Nov. 20 (Xinhua) -- Foreign direct investment (FDI) in China's high-tech industries posted robust year-on-year growth in the first 10 months of 2026, official data showed on Friday. FDI in high-tech industries reached 252.83 billion yuan (about 37.66 billion U.S. dollars) during the January-October period, up 31.3 percent year on year. It accounted for 41.7 percent of China's total FDI in actual use, increasing by 10.7 percentage points from the same period last year, according to the Ministry of Commerce. Specifically, FDI in aerospace and equipment manufacturing, services for the commercialization of sci-tech achievements, and electronic and telecommunications equipment manufacturing surged 128.8 percent, 73.3 percent and 35.7 percent, respectively. A total of 52,853 new foreign-invested enterprises were established nationwide during this period, down 1.7 percent year on year, while FDI in actual use stood at 606.93 billion yuan, declining 2.4 percent from a year earlier. China's manufacturing industry attracted 143.04 billion yuan in FDI in this period, while the service sector drew 450.38 billion yuan. During the same period, FDI from Canada, France, Switzerland and the United States grew by 105.7 percent, 35.1 percent, 23.5 percent and 9.6 percent, respectively, with investment via free ports included in these calculations, the ministry revealed. High-tech and high-value-added industries have increasingly become a key focus for foreign investors in China, a report released in September said. Multinational corporations are accelerating the establishment of R&D centers in China, positioning the country as a vital node in their global innovation networks, the report noted. item.title: Asia-Pacific Media Partnership officially launched
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-21
Asia-Pacific Media Partnership officially launched BEIJING, Nov. 21 (Xinhua) -- The Asia-Pacific Media Partnership (APMP), proposed by China's Xinhua News Agency, has been officially launched, with its first batch of members comprising 310 organizations from 41 countries and regions across the Asia-Pacific. At the opening ceremony of the Asia-Pacific Media Forum held on Sept. 5, more than 400 representatives from over 40 countries and regions, as well as from UN agencies and international organizations, witnessed the establishment of the Organizing Committee of the Asia-Pacific Media Partnership Program. The committee issued an initiative on strengthening collaborative communication between the media and think tanks, inviting media outlets and think tanks in the Asia-Pacific region to join the partnership. Aiming to strengthen mutually beneficial and win-win cooperation among media organizations across the Asia-Pacific region, the APMP focuses on building four key platforms: high-end dialogue, collaborative communication, technological innovation and pragmatic cooperation. It will regularly hold high-level media dialogues, promote joint interviews among Asia-Pacific media, jointly produce high-quality multimedia products, organize inbound reporting tours in China for Asia-Pacific media journalists, and host themed training programs for Asia-Pacific media professionals, among a series of practical cooperation projects. Both the APMP and the Shenzhen Consensus of the Asia-Pacific Media Forum have been officially included in the deliverables list for China's hosting of the 2026 Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) meetings. The Asia-Pacific Media Forum has also been included in the list of meetings and events hosted by China as the 2026 APEC host. Copyright © 2026 People's Daily Online. All Rights Reserved.

item.title: Xi's APEC speech inspires optimism for new chapter in Asia-Pacific prosperity
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-21
Xi's APEC speech inspires optimism for new chapter in Asia-Pacific prosperity This photo taken on Nov. 19, 2026 shows the International Communication Center of Shenzhen, the venue of the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting, in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province. (Xinhua/Xing Guangli) * "If the Asia-Pacific miracle of the past more than three decades was a story of economic growth achieved through openness and cooperation, the next 30 years should be a story of shared prosperity achieved through inclusiveness and win-win cooperation," said South Korean lawmaker Kim Tae-nyeon. * China's proposal to set up cooperation institutions focusing on the digital economy, clean energy and SME cooperation carries great significance and represents a key step in fostering new growth drivers for the Asia-Pacific, said Vitaly Mankevich, president of the Russian-Asian Union of Industrialists and Entrepreneurs. * Georgie Too Hann Huei, COO of the Malaysia-China Business Council in Kuala Lumpur, said China is not only an active practitioner in the digital economy, clean energy and the development of SMEs, but has also accumulated rich experience in these fields, noting that China is now translating its development experience into concrete actions to promote common regional development. SHENZHEN, Nov. 20 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping chaired the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen on Thursday, calling for further efforts to build an Asia-Pacific community and write a new chapter of the Asia-Pacific miracle. Experts said Xi's speech at the gathering outlined China's vision for a stronger, more integrated Asia-Pacific community, offering a roadmap for the region to build on the achievements of the past three decades. They also said it could help deepen regional cooperation, create new opportunities for shared development and contribute to peace, stability and prosperity in the Asia-Pacific and beyond. A SHARED VISION In his Thursday speech, Xi stressed that building an Asia-Pacific community requires solidarity and mutual assistance, openness and integration, enterprise and innovation, as well as inclusive development. These requirements are interconnected and mutually reinforcing, said Herbert Sima, director of the China Studies Center at the University of Auckland, noting they not only provide guidance for economic cooperation in the Asia-Pacific, but also offer valuable insights into addressing global uncertainties. Solidarity and mutual assistance form the foundation of cooperation, openness and connectivity provide a pathway for development, innovation and progress serve as the driving force for growth, while inclusive development is key to ensuring that cooperation is sustainable and benefits all parties, the expert explained. This photo taken on Nov. 3, 2026 shows a view of Shennan Avenue in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province. (Xinhua/Liang Xu) In his speech, Xi reviewed the achievements of the Asia-Pacific miracle over the past thirty-plus years, stressing the need to adapt to the new realities, take new strides and open up new prospects for Asia-Pacific cooperation in the face of new opportunities and challenges. Xi's remarks have prompted experts to again reflect on the factors behind the region's remarkable economic growth and the prospects for its future development. Virdika Rizky Utama, executive director of the Jakarta-based think tank PARA Syndicate, said the Asia-Pacific miracle had been driven by open cooperation, trade and investment, and the integration of regional industrial and supply chains. What Xi stressed about building the Asia-Pacific community offered a response to the challenges facing the region and a vision for future cooperation, he said. The expert particularly noted Xi's mention of "open regionalism" in his speech, saying that for developing economies such as Indonesia, the concept means access to broader markets and more convenient connectivity. Tran Thi Hai Yen, a researcher at the Institute for European and Americas Studies at Vietnam Academy of Social Sciences, said Xi's vision comes at a timely moment, which addresses the four practical needs currently facing the Asia-Pacific region. As the rotating chair of APEC this year, she added, China has further clarified the direction of cooperation and underscored the urgency of accelerating joint efforts, helping translate long-term vision into concrete cooperation agendas. History proves that economies can prosper through trade with one another, and Xi reaffirmed the value of trade cooperation and open regionalism, said Craig Emerson, director of the Australia APEC Study Center. A drone photo taken on Nov. 19, 2026 shows a ship arriving at Rizhao Port in east China's Shandong Province. (Xinhua/Guo Xulei) Such remarks are highly encouraging at a time when trade liberalization has faced growing skepticism in recent years, noted Emerson, a former Australian trade minister. "If the Asia-Pacific miracle of the past more than three decades was a story of economic growth achieved through openness and cooperation, the next 30 years should be a story of shared prosperity achieved through inclusiveness and win-win cooperation," said South Korean lawmaker Kim Tae-nyeon. "Economies in the Asia-Pacific region differ in terms of economic size, stages of development, history and culture, making the region highly diverse," he said. "This diversity should be regarded as a valuable resource. We should leverage our respective strengths, complement one another's weaknesses and turn these differences into new opportunities for cooperation." BUILDING PILLARS TOGETHER China is an advocate, promoter and forerunner in Asia-Pacific economic cooperation, and it is ready to work with all parties to pool wisdom and synergy in building the four key pillars of an Asia-Pacific community, Xi said in his speech. He also called for strengthening the pillar of economy and trade, upgrading the pillar of connectivity, fostering the pillar of innovation and enhancing the pillar of development. On the importance of connectivity, Alvaro Echeverria, director of the Asia Pacific Chamber of Commerce in Chile, said the call to upgrade the pillar of connectivity was particularly relevant in the current international environment. Greater proximity helps create mutual understanding, Echeverria told Xinhua, saying he welcomes China's call to strengthen connectivity not only through physical infrastructure, but also through continued efforts to promote human development and closer people-to-people exchanges. These efforts could help rebuild trust at a time when the world faces considerable uncertainty and a lack of predictability, while the need for international coordination continues to grow, he added. Xi pointed out that China is rooted in the Asia-Pacific and will continue to support Asia-Pacific cooperation, and announced that China will provide 20 million U.S. dollars to support APEC's practical cooperation, and to establish a Center for Asia-Pacific Community Studies in Shenzhen to conduct policy research and exchanges and provide intellectual support. In addition, Xi said that in line with the needs of Asia-Pacific cooperation, China will set up cooperation institutions in such areas as digital technology, cross-border data flow, clean energy, and the development of small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) to contribute to innovation-driven and green growth in the Asia-Pacific. A foreign journalist takes a cup of coffee made by a humanoid robot at the media center of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, Nov. 16, 2026. (Xinhua/Ren Pengfei) China's proposal to set up cooperation institutions focusing on the digital economy, clean energy and SME cooperation carries great significance and represents a key step in fostering new growth drivers for the Asia-Pacific, said Vitaly Mankevich, president of the Russian-Asian Union of Industrialists and Entrepreneurs. "As a recognized technology leader in the digital economy, clean energy and related sectors, China can use these cooperation bodies to advance pragmatic cooperation among Asia-Pacific economies and build science and technology innovation partnerships," Mankevich said. Georgie Too Hann Huei, COO of the Malaysia-China Business Council in Kuala Lumpur, said China is not only an active practitioner in the digital economy, clean energy and the development of SMEs, but has also accumulated rich experience in these fields, noting that China is now translating its development experience into concrete actions to promote common regional development. "This approach of 'getting its own house in order first and then bringing partners along' demonstrates China's leading role and exemplary influence in regional cooperation," he said. item.title: Shenzhen "peace summit" underscores shared responsibilities of major countries
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-21
Shenzhen "peace summit" underscores shared responsibilities of major countries BEIJING, Nov. 20 (Xinhua) -- The first-ever face-to-face meeting between the heads of state of China, Russia and the United States in Shenzhen sent a clear message at a time of mounting geopolitical tensions: the world needs major countries to build bridges, not barriers, and safeguard peace, not fuel confrontation. The historic meeting on Nov. 19, which Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi described as a "peace summit," saw the three leaders engage in candid, friendly and constructive exchanges on major issues concerning global peace, security and stability. It also produced a series of important consensuses and a declaration toward peace, demonstrating that even countries with differences can find common ground through dialogue. Yet some have sought to frame the meeting as "Yalta 2.0," drawing a flawed parallel with the 1945 gathering of the leaders of the Soviet Union, the United States and Britain that helped shape the postwar order. Such readings are rooted in the old mindset of power politics and spheres of influence, and ignore profound shifts in the global landscape. The circumstances and choices facing the world today are fundamentally different. The Shenzhen meeting was not about deciding the fate of other countries behind closed doors. Rather, it focused on how three major countries, despite their differences, could strengthen communication, manage disagreements and jointly safeguard peace and stability. Chinese President Xi Jinping made four points on how major countries could find the right way to get along and jointly underpin world peace, calling for mutual respect, peaceful coexistence, win-win cooperation, and dialogue and consultation. Together, they offer a constructive path for fostering sound major-country relations in a turbulent world. Mutual respect and peaceful coexistence should be firmly upheld. Nations differ in their social systems, histories, cultures and development paths. Such differences are an objective reality of international relations, not a license for confrontation or interference. No country should seek to impose its will on others, still less treat another country's legitimate development as a threat simply because it is growing stronger. Win-win cooperation is a practical necessity in a deeply interconnected world, rather than a mere diplomatic slogan. Global supply chains, trade and technological innovation link countries in ways that cannot be easily undone without imposing costs on all sides. Attempts to decouple economies, disrupt supply chains or erect barriers to technological cooperation may serve narrow geopolitical calculations, but they inevitably undermine shared development and weaken the foundations of global prosperity. No country can secure its own long-term development by denying others' legitimate right to develop. The choice before major countries is not between one country's success and another's, but between pursuing shared progress and allowing zero-sum rivalry to hold everyone back. Dialogue and consultation are equally indispensable. Major countries inevitably have differences, some of them deep and long-standing. The measure of responsible diplomacy is not whether these differences can be eliminated overnight, but whether they can be managed properly without escalating into confrontation. Maintaining regular high-level exchanges, keeping communication channels open and strengthening crisis-prevention mechanisms are therefore not optional gestures, but essential safeguards against miscalculation and conflict. This is particularly important because major countries bear far-reaching responsibilities. When major countries live in harmony, the world is at peace; when they fight, the world is thrown into turmoil. Their interactions affect not only bilateral ties, but also regional security, the global economy and prospects for peace across the world. China's vision of an equal and orderly multipolar world reflects this conviction. It's a world in which countries, regardless of size or strength, enjoy equal opportunities to participate in international affairs, differences are addressed through consultation rather than coercion, and international rules and institutions are upheld by all to serve the common interests of the international community. Viewed from this broader perspective, the significance of the Shenzhen meeting becomes clear. It did not erase the differences among the three countries, nor could a single meeting resolve every international challenge. Instead, its value lies in reaffirming the importance of sustained communication, identifying areas of common ground and creating more room for managing differences. At a time when mistrust and confrontation threaten to narrow the space for diplomacy, that is no small achievement. The world has already learned, at great cost, where division, confrontation and power politics can lead. What it needs now is not another attempt to carve up spheres of influence, but the political courage of major countries to respect one another, coexist peacefully and pursue the common interests of all humanity. The consensus reached by the three leaders should be translated into concrete actions to build a future shaped by dialogue, mutual respect and shared responsibility. item.title: Xi, Prabowo announce launch of China-Indonesia comprehensive economic partnership negotiations
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-20
Xi, Prabowo announce launch of China-Indonesia comprehensive economic partnership negotiations Chinese President Xi Jinping meets with Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, Nov. 20, 2026. Prabowo is in China for the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting, held from Wednesday to Thursday. (Xinhua/Li Xiang) SHENZHEN, Nov. 20 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping and Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto on Friday announced the launch of negotiations for a bilateral comprehensive economic partnership. The announcement was made during Xi's meeting with Prabowo in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province. Prabowo is in China for the 33rd APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting, held from Wednesday to Thursday. Xi said the two countries should strengthen strategic communication and solidarity, deepen all-round strategic cooperation, consolidate the foundation of political trust, and jointly guard against and respond to external risks. He called on both countries to expand mutually beneficial cooperation, advance major projects such as the Jakarta-Bandung High-Speed Railway, and deepen cooperation in energy and mineral resources, artificial intelligence, the digital economy, and clean energy. Xi called for efforts to reach an all-round, high-standard comprehensive economic partnership agreement at an early date. Amid emerging risks and challenges in the world, China is ready to strengthen coordination and cooperation with Indonesia within multilateral frameworks, including the United Nations, APEC and China-ASEAN cooperation, Xi said. Prabowo said Indonesia's strategic partnership with China is stronger than ever, reaffirming that Indonesia firmly adheres to the one-China policy and that Taiwan is a province of the People's Republic of China. Indonesia sincerely welcomes Chinese enterprises to invest and do business in the country, and is committed to providing a reliable, stable and predictable business environment, Prabowo said. Prabowo said Indonesia highly appreciates China's role as a responsible major country in international affairs, and stands ready to work with China to safeguard the shared interests of the Global South and promote regional and global peace and stability. item.title: Xi says China, Australia should be mutually trusted partners
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-20
Xi says China, Australia should be mutually trusted partners Chinese President Xi Jinping meets with Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, Nov. 20, 2026. Albanese is in China for the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting, held from Wednesday to Thursday. (Xinhua/Li Xiang) SHENZHEN, Nov. 20 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping said Friday that China and Australia should be cooperative partners who trust each other and help each other succeed, as the two countries have no historical grievances or conflicts of fundamental interests. China-Australia relations are stable at present, said Xi when meeting with Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province. Albanese is in China for the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting, held from Wednesday to Thursday. As next year marks the 55th anniversary of diplomatic relations between China and Australia, Xi called on the two sides to achieve greater progress in bilateral relations from a new starting point. Xi said that in a volatile and turbulent world, the two countries should enhance mutual trust, accommodate each other's core interests and major concerns, and keep to the right direction of friendship and cooperation. He called for deepening mutually beneficial cooperation in pursuit of the two countries' respective development goals, advancing traditional cooperation in agriculture, energy and minerals, and expanding cooperation in emerging areas such as the green economy, new energy, the digital industry, artificial intelligence (AI) and climate change response. Efforts should be made to promote friendship between the two countries through expanded people-to-people exchanges, Xi said, noting that the two sides had agreed to designate 2027 as the China-Australia Year of Tourism. He also emphasized the need to strengthen multilateral coordination in addressing global challenges, advance the building of an Asia-Pacific community, and jointly uphold the international system with the United Nations at its core and the international order based on international law. Albanese said that the improvement and development of Australia-China relations serves the interests of both sides and brings tangible benefits to the peoples of both countries. He said that Australia stands ready to maintain close high-level exchanges with China, strengthen practical cooperation in trade, investment, AI and other areas, deepen people-to-people exchanges, respect each other and properly handle differences, so as to make Australia-China relations an example for countries with different systems to develop constructive relations. item.title: Xi says China, Singapore should strengthen strategic communication, enhance coordination
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-20
Xi says China, Singapore should strengthen strategic communication, enhance coordination Chinese President Xi Jinping meets with Singaporean Prime Minister Lawrence Wong in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, Nov. 20, 2026. Wong is in China for the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting, held from Wednesday to Thursday. (Xinhua/Shen Hong) SHENZHEN, Nov. 20 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping said on Friday that China and Singapore should strengthen strategic communication and enhance solidarity and coordination as the world is undergoing accelerated changes unseen in a century. The two countries should be sincere friends who trust each other and support each other in pursuing development paths suited to their respective national conditions, said Xi when meeting with Singaporean Prime Minister Lawrence Wong in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province. Wong attended the 33rd APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting held from Wednesday to Thursday in Shenzhen. During the meeting, Xi called for advancing the all-round high-quality future-oriented partnership between China and Singapore to new heights, and stressed the need for both sides to advance high-quality Belt and Road cooperation. The two countries should launch negotiations for upgraded Version 4.0 of their free trade agreement, and deliver signature cooperation outcomes in areas such as the digital economy, green development, and artificial intelligence, Xi added. Noting that both countries should be "a progressive force" for championing international fairness and justice, Xi called for safeguarding regional peace and stability while jointly building an Asia-Pacific community and a community with a shared future for humanity. For his part, Wong stated that Singapore firmly adheres to the one-China policy and opposes "Taiwan independence." Singapore stands ready to work with China to enhance political mutual trust, deepen cooperation in areas such as trade, industrial and supply chains, and artificial intelligence, and promote people-to-people exchanges, the prime minister noted. Wong said Singapore is willing to strengthen communication and cooperation with the Chinese side on international affairs to jointly address global challenges. item.title: Xi calls for promoting building of a China-Thailand community with a shared future to higher level
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-20
Xi calls for promoting building of a China-Thailand community with a shared future to higher level Chinese President Xi Jinping meets with Thai Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, Nov. 20, 2026. Anutin is in China for the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting, held from Wednesday to Thursday. (Xinhua/Li Xiang) SHENZHEN, Nov. 20 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping on Friday called for promoting the building of a China-Thailand community with a shared future to a higher level. China and Thailand should continuously enhance political mutual trust and strengthen solidarity and coordination, Xi said when meeting with Thai Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province. The two countries should step up exchanges between governments, political parties, legislatures and at other levels, and safeguard their common strategic interests, Xi stressed. He called on the two sides to make good use of cooperation mechanisms in economy and trade, science and technology, and the digital economy, expand and strengthen traditional cooperation in agriculture and connectivity, and cultivate and strengthen new growth areas of cooperation such as artificial intelligence, new energy vehicles, aviation and aerospace, disaster prevention, mitigation and relief, and water resources management. The two sides should strengthen cooperation in culture, education, and tourism, Xi added. He also urged intensifying efforts to crack down on illegal and criminal activities such as online gambling and telecom fraud. The two sides should strengthen multilateral coordination and work together to safeguard the common interests of the Global South, Xi said. China is ready to play a positive role in bringing about an early turnaround in Thailand-Cambodia relations, Xi said. For his part, Anutin said Thailand is ready to continue to strengthen high-level exchanges with China and enhance cooperation in areas such as trade, investment, science and technology, industrial and supply chains, and connectivity. Thailand will resolutely crack down on cross-border crimes including online gambling and telecom fraud, and protect the safety of Chinese citizens in Thailand, he said, adding that the country welcomes more Chinese visitors. Anutin attended the 33rd APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen, held from Wednesday to Thursday.
